title: Natural Gas Grill Installation: Gas Line Tie-In, Fittings, and Leak Testing (Ask This Old House)
summary: This Old House walks through upgrading from a propane, hand-me-down grill to a natural-gas fed unit. The episode covers planning the gas-line run from the street, verifying capacity with the existing meter, and routing the line outside the building. It demonstrates both traditional threaded piping with pipe dope and a modern compression/O-ring connection for gas-tight seals, including offset elbows to correct alignment. A drip leg is installed to trap rust before it reaches the burner, followed by a soap-solution leak test. The video emphasizes consulting a licensed gas fitter and obtaining the necessary permit, and ends with a tour of the grill’s built-in features (pancake/waffle option, wok insert, beer-can chicken, pizza stone) and turning the grill on.
